title: "start request repeated too quickly" is systemd's own rate limiter, not a fresh crash
explanation: `systemctl start worker2` refuses outright with that message — it isn't the unit crashing again, it's `StartLimitIntervalSec=`/`StartLimitBurst=` in the unit having already tripped from earlier restart attempts. This means there are two separate things going on: whatever originally crashed the service, and systemd's own safety valve that kicked in afterward.

title: Find the original cause before touching the rate limiter
explanation: `journalctl -u worker2 -n 30 --no-pager` shows repeated `FATAL: missing /etc/worker2/worker2.conf` right before each restart. With `Restart=always` and a short `RestartSec=1`, the service crashed, systemd restarted it, it crashed again, several times, fast enough to hit `StartLimitBurst=3` within `StartLimitIntervalSec=20` — which is what latched the unit into start-limit-hit in the first place.

title: Fix the actual bug first
explanation: Creating `/etc/worker2/worker2.conf` with the `QUEUE_NAME=` line the script expects addresses the real crash cause. But doing only this and then trying `systemctl start worker2` still fails — the unit is latched in the failed, start-limited state independent of whether the underlying cause is now fixed.

title: Clear the failure counter explicitly
explanation: `systemctl reset-failed worker2` is the only thing that clears the start-limit-hit state — daemon-reload doesn't touch it, and simply waiting doesn't either unless you wait out the full `StartLimitIntervalSec` window. This two-step requirement (fix the cause, then reset-failed) is one of the most common "I fixed it but it still won't start" traps with systemd.

title: Start and verify
explanation: With both the config in place and the failure counter cleared, `systemctl start worker2` succeeds and `systemctl is-active worker2` reports `active` — and this time it stays that way, since the crash loop that originally tripped the limiter is actually gone, not just paused.
